modification (change to an organism)
przetworzenie, przerobienie

examples.text: Kalendarz gregoriański jest modyfikacją kalendarza juliańskiego.

glosses: zmiana

examples.text: Klimat obszaru Koszalina kształtują masy powietrza napływające znad Oceanu Atlantyckiego, których cechy ulegają modyfikacji za sprawą sąsiedztwa Morza Bałtyckiego i deniwelacji terenu na granicy Pobrzeża Południowobałtyckiego i Pojezierza Pomorskiego.

glosses: The form of existence belonging to a particular object, entity etc.; a mode of being.

examples.text: Pleasure is the business of woman's life, according to the present modification of society […]

glosses: the change undergone by a word when used in a construction (for instance am => 'm in I'm)
The result of modifying something; a new or changed form.
The act of making a change to something while keeping its essential character intact; an alteration or adjustment.

examples.text: behavior modification officer
Jim's modification to the radio's tuning resulted in clearer sound.

glosses: A change to an organism as a result of its environment that is not transmissable to offspring.

examples.text: Due to his sunbathing, Jim's body experienced modifications: he got a tan.

glosses: a change to a word when it is borrowed by another language

examples.text: The Chinese word "kòu tóu" had a modification made to become the English "kowtow".

glosses: Handlung oder Vorgang, etwas abzuändern, und Ergebnis dieser Handlung

examples.text: Es gilt noch einige Modifikationen an dem Entwurf vorzunehmen, bevor er in die Produktion geht.
„Jüngers Prozedere besteht mithin aus der Übernahme und Modifikation von Vorgaben und Einflüssen anderer Autoren.“

glosses: To become something different.

examples.text: The tadpole changed into a frog.
Stock prices are constantly changing.

glosses: To make something into something else.

examples.text:
Lo I the man, whoſe Muſe whilome did maske,
As time her taught in lowly Shepheards weeds,
Am now enforſt a far unfitter taske,
For trumpets ſterne to chaunge mine oaten reeds,
And ſinge of Knights and Ladies gentle deeds[…]

KORRIS: They shunned you. Cursed you. Called you vile names, and you knew not why. Even now do you know why you are driven? Why you cannot relent—or repent—or confess—or abstain? How could you know? There have been no other Klingons to lead you to that knowledge.
WORF: Yes—yes—those feelings are still a part of me, but I control them. They do not rule me.
KORRIS: Yes, to fit in, the humans demand you change the one thing that you cannot change. But because you cannot—you do. That too is the mark of the warrior.

Of all the transitions brought about on the Earth’s surface by temperature change, the melting of ice into water is the starkest. It is binary. And for the land beneath, the air above and the life around, it changes everything.

The fairy changed the frog into a prince.
I had to change the wording of the ad so it would fit.

glosses: To replace.

examples.text: Ask the janitor to come and change the lightbulb.
After a brisk walk, I washed up and changed my shirt.
Towards the end of the nineteenth century, boys who had pretended soldiers down through the centuries, now changed their pikes and swords for toy pistols.

glosses: To replace one's clothing.

examples.text: You can't go into the dressing room while she’s changing.
The clowns changed into their costumes before the circus started.

glosses: To replace the clothing of (the one wearing it), especially to put a clean diaper on (someone).

examples.text: It’s your turn to change the baby.

glosses: To transfer to another vehicle (train, bus, etc.)

examples.text: After stopping at these stations, my train has become busy. Returning day-trippers make up a goodly number, along with young people heading for a night out in Bristol, which is where I change once again.

glosses: To exchange.

examples.text: At the first sight / they have changed eyes. (exchanged looks)
I would give any thing to change a word or two with this person.

glosses: To change hand while riding (a horse).

examples.text: to change a horse

glosses: The process of becoming different.

examples.text: The product is undergoing a change in order to improve it.
Cause people often talk about being scared of change / But for me I'm more afraid of things staying the same

Of all the transitions brought about on the Earth’s surface by temperature change, the melting of ice into water is the starkest. It is binary. And for the land beneath, the air above and the life around, it changes everything.

glosses: Small denominations of money given in exchange for a larger denomination.

examples.text: Can I get change for this $100 bill, please?

glosses: A replacement.

examples.text: a change of clothes

After beating champions Chelsea 3-1 on Boxing Day, Arsenal boss Arsene Wenger made eight changes to his starting XI in an effort to freshen things up, with games against Birmingham and Manchester City to come in the next seven days.

glosses: Balance of money returned from the sum paid after deducting the price of a purchase.

examples.text: A customer who pays with a 10-pound note for a £9 item receives one pound in change.

glosses: An amount of cash, usually in the form of coins, but sometimes inclusive of paper money.

examples.text: Do you have any change on you? I need to make a phone call.
This bus ride requires exact change.

glosses: A transfer between vehicles.

examples.text: The train journey from Bristol to Nottingham includes a change at Birmingham.
It [the Elizabeth Line] will provide a 6tph (trains per hour) service and with a single change at Hayes & Harlington offer services towards Reading.

glosses: A change-up pitch.
Any order in which a number of bells are struck, other than that of the diatonic scale.

examples.text: Four bells admit twenty-four changes in ringing.

glosses: A public house; an alehouse.

examples.text:
1727-1728, Edward Burt, Letters from a Gentleman in the North of Scotland to his Friend in London
They call an alehouse a change.
